svg.title: Direct / Off / Reactive treble bleed
svg.desc: Builder wiring reference for the Direct / Off / Reactive treble bleed switch, revision 1.0, 2026-11-23, in eight numbered panels: what you are building, the stock volume and tone circuit, the finished circuit with the five changed wires numbered, the tone pot lugs from the rear, the switch contact map, the three modes, the bleed values by volume pot, and common ground with bench checks.
svg.text: DIRECT / OFF / REACTIVE TREBLE BLEED • WIRING REFERENCE
MATCH IDENTICAL BOXED WIRE LABELS • CONFIRM POT AND SWITCH LUGS WITH A METER
Shown on Relay Lipstick; fits any guitar with one master volume and one master tone wired this way
One three-position switch sets what the
treble bleed does as I turn the volume down.
An ordinary treble bleed: the highs stay as
No bleed. The tone knob works as usual.
The bleed follows the tone knob: roll the
tone back and the bleed eases off.
1. Find a spot near the tone pot where the
switch body clears the cavity, the pots and the
wiring, then drill one hole sized for your
switch (a common mini toggle needs 6 mm;
2. Rewire the tone pot: the BUS wire moves to
the wiper, and the 22 nF capacitor moves to the
3. Move the bleed's input end to the switch's
4. Add two wires: BUS to Direct, and the tone
An on–off–on mini toggle (SPDT), a bleed
volume wiper to the jack tip
tone CW end to the Reactive lug
bleed capacitor to the switch's Common
tone CCW end to the 22 nF capacitor
Colored wires carry their label's color;
Pots seen from the back, lugs down • values for a 500k volume pot
As it comes: the signal (BUS) reaches the tone pot at its CCW end, the tone wiper goes to the 22 nF capacitor, and the CW end isn't used.
The bleed, a resistor and a capacitor in series, runs from BUS to OUT. If your volume pot has no bleed, add one (panel 7).
Pots seen from the back, lugs down • switch in the middle (Off) position
The numbers mark the wires that move or are new:
1. The BUS wire moves to the tone wiper.
2. The 22 nF capacitor moves to the CCW end.
3. A new wire runs from the tone CW end to the Reactive lug.
4. The bleed's input end moves to the switch's Common lug.
5. A new wire runs from BUS to the switch's Direct lug.
Everything else stays as it was.
REAR VIEW • shaft away • lugs down
Makers number lugs differently: find the wiper and the
ends with a meter. The volume pot's wiring doesn't change.
An on–off–on mini toggle (SPDT) has three lugs: Common and two ends.
On many mini toggles, Common is the middle lug of the row.
The dashed circle shows where the lever rests in the middle position.
It is not a place on the part, and it touches nothing.
This is the idea, not the lug layout, so confirm with a meter on
continuity: Common beeps to the Direct lug in Direct, to the Reactive
lug in Reactive, and to nothing in Off.
How the switch connects the bleed; the glow shows its path
The lever joins Common to the Direct lug, so
the bleed meets the main signal wire (BUS). An
The lever rests on no lug, so the bleed is
disconnected. The tone knob works as usual.
The lever joins Common to the Reactive lug, so
the bleed is fed from the tone pot's CW end.
Roll the tone back and the bleed eases off.
The dashed circle is the middle rest position: no lug, so nothing is joined.
At tone 10, Reactive and Direct are the same circuit. At volume 10, all three modes are the same.
• Resistor: one standard step either way, meaning the next
value up or down in the usual resistor series
GND (ground) joins the volume pot's CCW lug, the 22 nF capacitor's free
end and the jack sleeve. The rest of the guitar's ground stays as it is.
1. Meter all three positions: Common to Direct in Direct, Common
to Reactive in Reactive, Common to nothing in Off.
2. Tone at 10: Direct and Reactive sound the same.
3. Volume at 10: all three modes sound the same.
4. The switch is quiet when I change modes.
5. The switch still clears the cavity, the pots and the wiring.
6. Match the loudness, then compare the modes at volume 5, tone 5
7. Sweep both knobs in each mode.
